paras: The Rockdale County posse killing was the fatal shooting of an unnamed Black man by a posse in Rockdale County, Georgia, reported from Atlanta on November 23, 1881. The man, accused of robbing a store, was shot dead after he refused an order to stop, and a jury returned a verdict of justifiable homicide. The brief dispatch ran in papers from Georgia to Texas and Pennsylvania, which headed it variously as a robber's death or as "justifiable homicide."

According to the Atlanta dispatch, a man described as "a negro" had robbed a store in Rockdale County and then tried to escape. A posse that was chasing him ordered him to stop; in the posse's account he refused and attempted to draw his pistol. The posse then fired at him, "killing him instantly." The reports give neither his name, the town or store involved, the date of the shooting, nor the number or names of the posse members.

A jury returned a verdict of justifiable homicide, which most copies of the dispatch reported in its closing sentence. No report of arrests, further inquiry or any response from Black residents appears in the coverage.

Every report was a near-verbatim copy of the same Atlanta telegram, so the posse's version and the jury's finding stood without any independent account. The Washington Evening Star printed it first, on November 23, under the headline "'Justifiable Homicide' in Georgia," setting the verdict in quotation marks. The next day the Savannah Morning News called it "A Negro Burglar Killed" and the Dallas Daily Herald "A Negro Robber Killed," leading with the man's race and alleged crime.

Other papers framed it through the shooters or the verdict: the Richmond Dispatch headed it "Shot by a Sheriff's Posse," the only copy to tie the posse to a sheriff, while the Knoxville Daily Chronicle used "Justifiable Homicide" and dated the dispatch November 22. The item kept circulating into December, in the Jackson Weekly Clarion's column of telegraphic briefs, the Dallas Weekly Herald, and the Somerset Herald in Pennsylvania under the title "The Fate of a Thief." None of these papers added comment, and no Georgia report with local detail was found.

reader.title: Rockdale County posse killing (1881)
bases: Every report describes a posse chasing an alleged store robber who was shot dead when he refused to stop, with no crowd, seizure from custody or ritual (A2, A3, A4).

A Black man accused of robbing a store was shot dead by a pursuing posse whose size is not given, and a jury found the killing justifiable homicide (A2, A3, A7). The only version is the posse's own account as carried by one Atlanta wire item, so legality rests on that claim and the jury's verdict (A2, A5).
All copies reproduce one Atlanta wire dispatch nearly word for word, with no local or independent account (A2, A3, A4, A6, A7).

accounts.label: Atlanta wire report (posse's version)
accounts.gist: A Black man who had robbed a store tried to escape, refused the posse's order to stop and tried to draw a pistol, and the posse fired and killed him instantly; a jury found it justifiable homicide.

framing.detail: Texas and Georgia papers headed the item 'A Negro Robber Killed' and 'A Negro Burglar Killed', naming the man by race and alleged crime.
The Washington Evening Star headed it '"Justifiable Homicide" in Georgia', setting the verdict in quotation marks.

The Richmond Dispatch ('Shot by a Sheriff's Posse'), Knoxville Daily Chronicle ('Justifiable Homicide'), Jackson Weekly Clarion and Somerset Herald ('The Fate of a Thief') carried the wire text without comment.

conflicts.note: Most copies date the dispatch November 23; the Knoxville copy's November 22 may be a typesetting slip. Neither dates the killing itself.

record_check.dossier: On or before 1881-11-23 (Atlanta dispatch dated Nov. 23; one copy says Nov. 22)
A pursuing posse, called a sheriff's posse in one headline; members unnamed
Not a lynching on the reported facts (posse killing in pursuit ruled justifiable homicide), resting on the posse's version only

info: On or before November 23, 1881 (exact date of the killing not given); the Knoxville copy is datelined November 22
